title: Three risk-profile portfolio templates
source: 04-investment-strategy/INVESTMENT_DECISION_FRAMEWORK.md, section 3 'Three risk-profile portfolios (concrete, cheap, no exotic access)', lines 106-145
account_currency_note: All instruments should be the cheapest available in the account's currency; for a Canadian account that means CDR/ETF equivalents where the FX spread is otherwise 1.75%.
rebalance_rule: Rebalance on bands (+/-5% absolute), not on a calendar, and never on a signal from this programme until something passes G1-G5.

portfolios.name: Stable / low-risk
portfolios.rationale: At 4.3% risk-free, a stable portfolio's job is not to lose, and 20% equity is the smallest allocation that still beats inflation over a decade.

sleeves.instrument: 1-12 month bills, or HISA at the best posted rate

portfolios.name: Moderate
portfolios.rationale: Close to the 60/40 shape. The P03-style book-level trend overlay is the only combination in this programme that improved risk-adjusted return and cut drawdown 77%, and it only worked because both legs had positive standalone expectancy.

portfolios.name: Aggressive
portfolios.rationale: Aggression is achieved with more beta, not with more trading. Every measured cost-bearing strategy in this estate destroyed value; leverage or option overlays would compound that.

sleeves.instrument: sized to be lost, not traded
